name: Skin Color Drift
description: Analyzes skin color drift patterns across frames
algorithm: Skin Color Drift — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method detects temporal skin color drift for deepfake detection:

1. **Skin Color Extraction**: Per-frame skin color is measured in perceptually uniform color space (CIE Lab) from multiple facial regions: forehead, cheeks, nose, chin. The color metrics — L* (lightness), a* (redness), b* (yellowness) — provide a comprehensive skin color characterization.

2. **Temporal Color Stability**: Skin color temporal signals are analyzed for stability. Natural skin color changes slowly (blood flow variations, ~0.1 Hz cardiac cycle, slower vasodilation). The method detects high-frequency color fluctuations inconsistent with physiological rates — deepfake generators may produce frame-to-frame color variations from inconsistent face rendering.

3. **Face-Neck Color Coherence**: Skin color should be consistent between face and neck regions over time (same person, same blood flow). The method tracks face-neck color difference. Deepfake face generation produces a face with potentially different skin color characteristics than the original neck, and this mismatch may vary over time.

4. **Illumination-Independent Color Analysis**: Skin color changes due to illumination are separated from intrinsic skin color changes using chromaticity-based methods. The method isolates the intrinsic skin color signal — physiological changes (blushing, pallor) have specific spectral signatures different from illumination changes. AI-generated color drift may show spectrally incorrect color variations.

5. **Cross-Region Color Correlation**: Different facial skin regions should show correlated color changes (same blood supply). The method checks inter-region color correlation — low correlation suggests different processing/generation of different face regions, characteristic of some deepfake methods.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through skin color drift analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
